clue.text: Dance written by Ireland to a danseuse

indicators.note: something written by another thing sits right beside it, so the pieces are set side by side

blocks.note: a ball is a formal dance
Erin is a poetic name for Ireland
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dance piece composed in Ireland and dedicated to a female dancer.
explanation.definitionFit: Danseuse is the French word for a female dancer, especially one in classical ballet companies.

clue.text: Miserable nark's state in America

blocks.note: feeling blue means feeling low or sad
both are British slang for a police informer

explanation.surface: A gloomy police informer's life in some American state.
explanation.walkthrough: A nark and a grass are both informers in British slang; to grass is to tell tales to the police.
explanation.definitionFit: Kentucky is nicknamed the Bluegrass State, so the name stands for that American state.

clue.text: Poet, student or accountant

blocks.note: L is a learner, as on British learner-driver plates
taken as written
CA is a chartered accountant

explanation.surface: A list of possible occupations: poet, student or accountant.
explanation.walkthrough: The commas suggest three alternatives; really the first word is the definition and the rest build the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Federico García Lorca was a celebrated Spanish poet and playwright of the twentieth century.

clue.text: It is used for shelling before the soldiers go in

definitions.text: It is used for shelling before the soldiers go in

blocks.clueFragment: shelling before the soldiers go in
blocks.note: surface reading: an artillery bombardment ahead of an infantry assault
setter's reading: a breakfast utensil for taking the top off a boiled egg, before strips of toast are dipped in

explanation.surface: A military weapon used to bombard positions before troops advance.
explanation.walkthrough: Soldiers are, in Britain, thin strips of toast dipped into a soft-boiled egg.
explanation.definitionFit: This small spoon is used to crack and scoop a boiled egg, so its shell is broken first.

clue.text: Difference in pitch produces a break

blocks.note: first meaning: the musical gap between two notes
second meaning: a pause between the acts of a show

explanation.surface: A change in musical pitch causes a pause in the performance.
explanation.definitionFit: In music the term names the distance between two notes; in theatres it names the mid-show pause.

clue.text: How's that for an attraction?

blocks.note: first meaning: the cricketers' cry asking the umpire for a batsman to be given out
second meaning: allure or charm

explanation.surface: Someone showing off something attractive and asking for approval.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, fielders shout "How's that?" (often "Howzat!") to ask the umpire to rule a batsman out.
explanation.definitionFit: The cricketers' shout is formally called this, and the same noun means charm or allure.

clue.text: Managed to put finishing touch to wall

blocks.note: first meaning: got by, dealt with a difficulty
second meaning: laid the sloping top course, called coping, along a wall

explanation.surface: A builder succeeding in completing a wall.
explanation.walkthrough: Coping is the capping layer of stone or brick on top of a wall; to lay it is a verb in its own right.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both getting through difficulties and capping masonry with its protective top layer.

clue.text: Yellow plate

blocks.note: first meaning: a bright yellow pigment made from lead chromate
second meaning: a shiny metallic coating applied by electroplating

explanation.surface: A yellow dish or plate.
explanation.definitionFit: The pigment chrome yellow and shiny chromium plating on cars both carry this short name.

clue.text: Put heroic creation in “A Gentleman of Verona”

indicators.note: a creation is something newly made up, so the letters are fashioned into a new word

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Placing a heroic character in Shakespeare's Two Gentlemen of Verona.
explanation.walkthrough: The quoted title nudges towards Two Gentlemen of Verona, but the man meant comes from The Taming of the Shrew.
explanation.definitionFit: In The Taming of the Shrew, Petruchio introduces himself as a gentleman from Verona who woos Katherina.

clue.text: He was capped while still at school

definitions.text: He was capped while still at school

blocks.clueFragment: He was capped while still at school
blocks.note: surface reading: a schoolboy sportsman picked for his national team
setter's reading: made to wear the pointed paper hat given to a slow pupil

explanation.surface: A schoolboy prodigy chosen to play for his country.
explanation.walkthrough: A cap in British sport is a selection for the national side.
explanation.definitionFit: A slow pupil was once made to wear a conical paper hat, the badge of a poor learner.

clue.text: Just one on either side of the keeper

definitions.text: one on either side of the keeper

blocks.note: first meaning: honest and fair

blocks.clueFragment: one on either side of the keeper
blocks.note: second meaning: a goalpost standing to each side of the goalkeeper

explanation.surface: Merely a player standing beside the goalkeeper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just' reads like 'only'; it is the adjective meaning righteous.
explanation.definitionFit: An honest person is described with this adjective, and each vertical goalpost is also called by this noun.

clue.text: Strait-laced girl enters into the joke

indicators.note: to enter into something is to go inside it, so one piece sits within another

blocks.note: a girl's name
a pun is a play on words

explanation.surface: A prim young woman manages to get involved in the joke after all.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone strait-laced is morally strict and prudish, like the Puritans of the seventeenth century.

clue.text: Hold note to file

blocks.note: G is a musical note
a rasp is a coarse file

explanation.surface: An instruction to keep a memo back to be filed away.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold something tightly in the hand is to seize or clutch it.

clue.text: Bat gets a black eye to nurse for a start

indicators.note: for a start says the nursing word comes first, at the front of the answer

blocks.note: to rear is to raise or nurture
slang for a bruised, swollen eye

explanation.surface: A bruiser gets a shiner and needs nursing back to health.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a dialect name for a bat; a mouse is old slang for a black eye.
explanation.definitionFit: This old dialect word names the flying mammal, literally a mouse that flutters.

clue.text: Confused to a great degree through illness

indicators.note: confused letters are jumbled up out of their proper order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Greatly bewildered because of being ill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to a great degree' reads as one phrase meaning 'very much'; it splits after 'great'.
explanation.definitionFit: At British universities this unclassified degree is granted to a candidate too ill to sit final exams.

clue.text: It's growing late for embarkation

blocks.note: first meaning: time passing, the hour advancing
second meaning: boarding a ship, bus or train

explanation.surface: Time is running out for passengers to board.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb describes the hour advancing or age creeping up, and also climbing aboard a vehicle.

clue.text: Note Henry's pulse

blocks.note: D is a musical note
Hal is a short form of Henry, with 's read as 'is'

explanation.surface: A doctor noting a patient's pulse rate.
explanation.walkthrough: Pulse here is the food, edible seeds such as lentils, not a heartbeat.
explanation.definitionFit: Pulses are lentils, peas and beans; this Indian dish or ingredient is made of split lentils.

clue.text: Distinctive feature of a maiden in Tenniel original

indicators.note: an original version is a fresh, newly made one, so the letters come out rearranged
in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: taken as written
M is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for a maiden over
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A characteristic trait of a girl in a drawing by Sir John Tenniel, illustrator of Alice.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a characteristic line or contour, especially of the face, hence a distinctive trait.

clue.text: Hen perhaps spotted beetle

blocks.note: first meaning: a female bird, as two words
second meaning: the small red insect with black spots

explanation.surface: A hen, it seems, has caught sight of a beetle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spotted' reads as 'seen'; it describes the beetle's markings.
explanation.definitionFit: A hen is a female or lady bird, and the familiar red spotted beetle also has that name.

clue.text: Sound this as you pass Acton, perhaps?

blocks.note: to pass something is to hand it over
Acton Bell was the pen name of Anne Brontë

explanation.surface: A sound to make while travelling past Acton, a district of west London.
explanation.walkthrough: Acton looks like the London district; it is the first name of Anne Brontë's pseudonym, Acton Bell.
explanation.definitionFit: This small bell held by its handle is something one rings, as town criers and school porters did.

clue.text: Son — could be the third

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for son
the archaic third-person verb ending, as in 'goeth'

explanation.surface: A genealogy note that a son might be the third in line.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue describes Adam's third son; read in parts, it gives the abbreviation for son followed by the old verb ending of the third person singular.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis this man is the third son born to Adam and Eve, after Cain and Abel.

clue.text: Sort of currant, say, in plum cake

indicators.note: say means as spoken, so the written word stands for another spelling that sounds the same
one thing being in another means it is placed inside it, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: currant sounds like current, and alternating current is one sort of electric current
plum and maroon are both deep purplish-red colours

explanation.surface: A baker identifying the kind of currant found in a plum cake.
explanation.walkthrough: The currants belong in the cake only on the surface; the sound gives an electrical current, abbreviated AC, which sits after the first letter of the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A macaroon is a small sweet biscuit or cake made from ground almonds or coconut with egg white.

clue.text: Gogol's characters include one woman's man

indicators.note: characters are the letters of the name, taken loose and rearranged
to include something is to take it inside

blocks.note: the Russian author's name, letter by letter
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Among the Russian novelist Gogol's characters is a ladies' man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'characters' looks like people in Gogol's novels; it means the letters of his name.
explanation.definitionFit: A man kept or paid by a woman as a companion or lover is literally a woman's man.

clue.text: Monstrous woman to note in biblical kingship

indicators.note: in places the musical note inside the outer pair

blocks.note: Og was King of Bashan in the Old Testament, and SS stands for steamship
re is the second note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A fearsome queen whose memory is written into the Bible's story of kingship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kingship' reads as one word; it splits into 'king' and 'ship'.
explanation.definitionFit: The female form of the folk-tale giant is a monstrous woman, often a fierce or frightening one.

clue.text: How Samuel helped himself?

blocks.note: surface reading: the way some man called Samuel took things for himself
setter's reading: Samuel Smiles, the Victorian author of the book Self-Help, did so in his own manner

explanation.surface: Asking how a man named Samuel served himself.
explanation.walkthrough: Samuel Smiles wrote Self-Help (1859), so his way of helping himself is turned into an adverb from his surname.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb describes doing something with a cheerful grin, punning on the surname of the Self-Help author.

clue.text: A place of changing moods

indicators.note: changing means altering, so the letters are put into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A location where people's tempers keep shifting.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical city destroyed for its wickedness alongside Gomorrah is a named location.

clue.text: On the way back, notice tea in country house

indicators.note: travelling back means going the opposite direction, so the word is read from right to left

blocks.note: an ad is a notice in a newspaper
cha is a slang word for tea

explanation.surface: Spotting a tearoom while returning to a country house.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the notice word turns round; the tea follows unchanged.
explanation.definitionFit: A dacha is a Russian country house or summer villa, typically used at weekends.

clue.text: A cold fish to embrace

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
the ling is a long fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: An unfriendly, unfeeling person who has to give someone a hug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cold fish' looks like a phrase for an aloof person; split it into two separate parts.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold someone tightly in one's arms is to hug or clasp them closely.

clue.text: Damned setter has disappeared!

blocks.note: a setter is a breed of gun dog
something that has disappeared is no longer here

explanation.surface: An exasperated cry that the crossword setter has vanished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setter' invites the compiler; here it is the dog breed.
explanation.definitionFit: This American exclamation is a mild euphemism for cursed, used as an expletive adjective.

clue.text: Detail in bit of news is an eye-opener

indicators.note: an opener is what comes first, so only the start of that word is used

blocks.note: a news item is a single story
taken as written
the opening letter of eye

explanation.surface: Something in a news report is surprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eye-opener' looks like a surprise; split it into the eye and its opener.
explanation.definitionFit: To list things one by one, specifying each part, is to set out every particular.

clue.text: Often pickled, servant has to leave

blocks.note: a man is a manservant
to go is to depart

explanation.surface: A servant who is frequently drunk is dismissed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pickled' suggests drunk; the definition describes a fruit used in chutneys and pickles.
explanation.definitionFit: This tropical fruit is commonly preserved in spiced vinegar as an Indian pickle or chutney.

clue.text: Portray separately incidental information

indicators.note: taken separately, this verb splits at its natural break into two short words, each clued on its own

blocks.note: port is the left-hand side of a ship
a ray is a beam of light

explanation.surface: An instruction to depict something piece by piece, alongside some background facts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Portray' reads as one verb; split into 'Port' and 'ray', each half supplies a word.
explanation.definitionFit: A sidelight is a piece of extra, indirect information that throws light on a subject from the side.
